title: Knowledge check: Alternative Representations and Content Negotiation

questions.prompt: What is the safest way to evolve a JSON representation?
options: Specify stable field names and types, decide null/missing behavior, and omit internal or sensitive fields by default.
Serialize every database column so clients have maximum flexibility.
Switch numbers, strings, and booleans between responses without a contract change.
Treat null, a missing property, and an empty collection as interchangeable in every context.
questions.answer_key: Specify stable field names and types, decide null/missing behavior, and omit internal or sensitive fields by default.
questions.explanation: Specify stable field names and types, decide null/missing behavior, and omit internal or sensitive fields by default. This is especially relevant to “Alternative Representations and Content Negotiation” because the API contract must remain explicit and reviewable.

questions.prompt: For the lesson “Alternative Representations and Content Negotiation”, which check provides the strongest practical evidence?
options: Rely on a code review comment without running any representative check.
Run one happy-path call and skip invalid, denied, and failure scenarios.
Test against production records so the exercise cannot be repeated safely.
Validate the JSON schema, types, nullability, and omission of restricted fields.
questions.answer_key: Validate the JSON schema, types, nullability, and omission of restricted fields.
questions.explanation: A useful check is repeatable, tied to an observable contract, and includes an important negative or boundary scenario.

questions.prompt: Which review warning is most relevant to “Alternative Representations and Content Negotiation”?
options: A representative test can reproduce the result.
The API avoids exposing internal secrets and personal data.
Public representation fields expose internal data or change meaning without review.
The expected behavior and relevant failure cases are documented.
questions.answer_key: Public representation fields expose internal data or change meaning without review.
questions.explanation: This finding weakens a core API guarantee and should be treated as a design or release issue, not only a style concern.
